body.en: An official commission of inquiry was set up, with Gandhi as the sole representative of the peasants. The planters agreed to refund money to the peasants, and Gandhi accepted twenty-five per cent. He explained that the amount mattered less than the fact that the planters had been obliged to surrender part of the money and their prestige. Within a few years the British planters gave up their estates, which went back to the peasants, and indigo sharecropping disappeared.

body.en: Gandhi did not stop at the legal victory. With volunteers, he opened primary schools in six villages; Kasturba taught cleanliness, and a doctor volunteered to treat the sick. Gandhi refused C. F. Andrews's offer to stay and help, because depending on an Englishman would show weakness: the peasants had to learn to rely on themselves. The real lesson was freedom from fear.
